name: OpenAI
short_description: Developer of GPT and the ChatGPT assistant, a leading frontier AI research lab.
why_relevant: Definition of the modern AI race; its model family is used by developers worldwide.
history: OpenAI was founded in San Francisco in December 2015 by Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Greg Brockman, Ilya Sutskever and others as a non-profit research lab. It released GPT-1 in 2018 and GPT-2 in 2019, then shifted in 2019 to a capped-profit structure backed by a $1 billion Microsoft investment. ChatGPT launched in November 2022 and reached 100 million users within two months. GPT-4 followed in 2023, and a $6.6 billion round in 2024 valued the company above $150 billion.

name: Anthropic
short_description: Maker of the Claude model family, focused on AI safety and interpretability.
why_relevant: Sets the safety-first alternative in frontier AI with enterprise adoption.
history: Anthropic was founded in San Francisco in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers Dario and Daniela Amodei and colleagues, with safety and interpretability as its core mission. It introduced Constitutional AI and launched Claude in March 2023. Google invested roughly $300 million in 2023 and Amazon committed up to $4 billion. The Claude 3 and Claude 3.5 families later became widely used enterprise models, and by 2024 the company was valued above $18 billion.

name: Google DeepMind
short_description: AI research lab behind AlphaFold, AlphaGo and the Gemini model family.
technology: Reinforcement learning, deep learning, protein folding
why_relevant: Won Nobel-level recognition for AI science; AlphaFold transformed biology.
history: DeepMind was founded in London in 2010 by Demis Hassabis, Shane Legg and Mustafa Suleyman, and was acquired by Google in 2014. It made history in 2016 when AlphaGo defeated Go champion Lee Sedol. AlphaFold then solved protein folding prediction, earning Hassabis and John Jumper the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. In 2023 DeepMind merged with Google Brain to form Google DeepMind, which released the Gemini model family and remains one of the world's leading frontier research labs.

name: Mistral AI
short_description: European developer of open-weight large language models and coding assistants.
why_relevant: Europe's flagship AI champion offering open-weight alternatives to closed labs.
history: Mistral AI was founded in Paris in May 2023 by Arthur Mensch, Guillaume Lample and Timothée Lacroix, former Meta and DeepMind researchers. It raised €105 million just weeks after launch and released the open-weight Mistral 7B model. A $415 million round followed in December 2023, valuing the company near $2 billion with Microsoft participating. It later launched the Mixtral mixture-of-experts models and the Le Chat assistant, becoming Europe's flagship AI champion.

name: Cohere
short_description: Builds multilingual LLMs and retrieval systems tailored for enterprises.
why_relevant: Pioneered retrieval-augmented generation for business-critical AI.
history: Cohere was founded in Toronto in 2019 by Aidan Gomez, Ivan Zhang and Nick Frosst, building on Gomez's co-authorship of the Transformer paper. It focused on enterprise-grade language models instead of consumer products and pioneered retrieval-augmented generation. The company raised hundreds of millions of dollars, reaching a $5.5 billion valuation in 2024, and serves major enterprise customers with its Command models and embedding platforms.

name: Hugging Face
short_description: Hosts the largest open repository of ML models, datasets and the Transformers library.
why_relevant: The default neutral hub for open weights and research artifacts.
history: Hugging Face was founded in New York in 2016 by Clément Delangue, Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf, originally as a chatbot startup. It pivoted in 2018 to open-source ML by releasing the Transformers library and then the Hugging Face Hub. The platform became the default home for open models, datasets and demos, hosting millions of artifacts. It raised over $395 million, reaching a $4.5 billion valuation in 2023, and partners with every major AI lab.

name: Perplexity AI
short_description: Builds an answer engine that searches the web with cited sources in real time.
why_relevant: Created the cited-answer search category and reshaped consumer search.
history: Perplexity AI was founded in San Francisco in 2022 by Aravind Srinivas, Denis Yarats, Johnny Ho and Andy Konwinski, aiming to reinvent web search with cited sources. Its answer engine launched publicly in December 2022 and grew rapidly through 2023. A Series B in early 2024 valued the company near $1 billion, followed by a $500 million round at a reported $9 billion valuation. It later launched the Comet browser to expand its consumer footprint.

name: xAI
short_description: Developer of the Grok assistant and the Colossus supercomputer.
why_relevant: Pushed large-scale training throughput in a short timeframe.
history: xAI was founded in 2023 by Elon Musk and a team of former OpenAI, DeepMind and Google researchers. It launched Grok in November 2023 and rapidly built the Colossus supercomputer in Memphis with 100,000 Nvidia H100 GPUs. The company raised $6 billion in 2024 and additional funding in 2025, reaching a reported valuation above $50 billion, while integrating Grok into X and aggressively expanding training throughput.

name: DeepSeek
short_description: Developer of open-weight reasoning models that rival frontier labs at low cost.
why_relevant: Demonstrated that frontier-competitive models can be trained efficiently.
history: DeepSeek was founded in 2023 in Hangzhou by Liang Wenfeng, backed by the quantitative fund High-Flyer. It released its open DeepSeek Coder and DeepSeek-V2 models, known for efficient mixture-of-experts designs. In January 2025 it launched DeepSeek-R1, a reasoning model trained at a fraction of frontier costs, which triggered global attention and a sharp market reaction. The company remains a leading force in open-weight, cost-efficient AI.

name: Moonshot AI
short_description: Developer of the Kimi assistant known for long-context understanding.
why_relevant: Leading long-context consumer assistant in China.
history: Moonshot AI was founded in Beijing in March 2023 by Yang Zhilin, a former Google and Meta researcher. It launched the Kimi assistant, notable for very long context windows, which quickly attracted millions of users in China. The company raised over $1 billion across rounds, including from Alibaba and Tencent, reaching a valuation above $3 billion by 2024, and remains a leading long-context consumer AI player.

name: Zhipu AI
short_description: Builds the GLM open model family and an AI developer platform.
why_relevant: Among China's leading open-model developers with broad app adoption.
history: Zhipu AI was founded in Beijing in 2019, tracing its roots to Tsinghua University's knowledge engineering lab. It developed the GLM family of open models and the ChatGLM assistant, becoming one of China's earliest LLM developers. Backed by Alibaba, Tencent and others, it raised substantial funding and launched an open developer platform. It was among the first Chinese AI firms to pursue a public listing, while continuing to expand its open-model ecosystem.

name: MiniMax
short_description: Develops text, voice and video models including the Hailuo video generator.
why_relevant: Pushes consumer multimodal generation at global scale.
history: MiniMax was founded in Shanghai in 2021 by Yan Junjie and colleagues, focusing on multimodal generation. It built the abab text models, the Hailuo video generator and audio tools widely used in China. The company raised funding from Alibaba, Tencent and other investors and reached a multi-billion-dollar valuation. It then pursued a Hong Kong IPO, positioning itself among China's top generative AI startups.

name: Scale AI
short_description: Supplies high-quality training data and labeling for AI systems.
why_relevant: The infrastructure layer behind most frontier AI data operations.
history: Scale AI was founded in San Francisco in 2016 by Alexandr Wang and Lucy Guo, providing data labeling and annotation for AI. It became the go-to data infrastructure partner for autonomous driving, defense and frontier labs, powering RLHF pipelines. In 2024 it raised a $1 billion round at a $13.8 billion valuation. In 2025 Meta invested roughly $14.3 billion for a 49% stake, and Wang joined Meta to lead its superintelligence efforts.

name: Cerebras Systems
short_description: Builds the wafer-scale engine for large AI training and inference.
why_relevant: Alternative high-bandwidth compute for frontier-scale training.
history: Cerebras Systems was founded in 2015 in Sunnyvale by Andrew Feldman and colleagues, betting on wafer-scale silicon. It unveiled the WSE chip in 2019, the largest semiconductor ever built, targeting AI training. Its wafer-scale design keeps memory on-chip to avoid interconnect bottlenecks. The company moved toward a public listing on Nasdaq during 2024-2025 and supplies high-bandwidth compute for training and inference, including to sovereign AI programs.

name: Groq
short_description: Runs a super-fast language processing unit for LLM inference.
why_relevant: Delivered order-of-magnitude faster LLM token throughput.
history: Groq was founded in 2016 in Mountain View by Jonathan Ross, a former Google TPU engineer. It developed the Language Processing Unit, a deterministic chip for very fast LLM inference. Public demos in 2024 showed token throughput far above GPU-based systems. The company raised over $640 million and reached a $2.8 billion valuation, later launching its own GroqCloud inference service for developers.

name: Together AI
short_description: Serverless cloud for open-source model training and inference.
why_relevant: Popular affordable inference runtime for the open-model ecosystem.
history: Together AI was founded in San Francisco in 2022 by Vipul Ved Prakash, Ce Zhang and Peri Mehrdad, building on open-source research. It offers a serverless cloud for training and serving open models, plus GPU clusters for enterprises. The company raised a $102.5 million Series A and later a $305 million round in 2025 at a reported $3.3 billion valuation, becoming a key runtime for the open-model ecosystem.

name: Anyscale
short_description: Creator of Ray, the distributed compute engine for scaling Python and AI workloads.
why_relevant: Ray underpins much of modern ML infrastructure.
history: Anyscale was founded in San Francisco in 2019 by Robert Nishihara, Philipp Moritz and Ion Stoica to commercialize Ray, the distributed computing framework. It evolved from UC Berkeley's RISELab and made Ray the backbone of many ML platforms. The company raised over $250 million, reaching a valuation above $1 billion in 2021, and expanded into managed Ray services for scaling AI workloads.

name: Modal
short_description: Serverless platform for running GPU and CPU compute workloads.
why_relevant: Made ephemeral parallel GPU jobs trivial to operate.
history: Modal was founded in San Francisco in 2021 by Erik Bernhardsson and Akshat Bubna to make serverless GPU compute effortless. Its platform lets developers run containerized Python functions on demand, scaling from zero to thousands of GPUs. It grew quickly among AI startups and researchers and raised a $25 million Series A and an $87 million Series B in 2025, becoming a popular ephemeral compute layer for AI.

name: Baseten
short_description: Infrastructure for building and serving AI applications in production.
why_relevant: Simplified path from fine-tuning to production serving.
history: Baseten was founded in 2019 by Tuhin Srivastava, Amir Haghighat and Parnas Sadau to simplify deploying ML models. It provides infrastructure to fine-tune, serve and scale models in production with an emphasis on inference performance. The company raised $40 million in 2024 and later a $75 million round, becoming a common serving layer for AI applications and agentic products. It also supports model performance optimization and GPU orchestration for demanding workloads.

name: Fireworks AI
short_description: Fast inference serving for open-source and custom models.
why_relevant: High-throughput open-model serving stack widely used by startups.
history: Fireworks AI was founded in 2022 in Redwood City by former Meta PyTorch engineers including Lin Qiao and Dmytro Ivchenko. It delivers high-throughput, low-latency inference for open-source and custom models through an optimized serving stack. The company raised a $52 million round in 2024 and a $250 million Series C in 2025 at a $4 billion valuation, serving many startups and enterprises.

name: Reka AI
short_description: Builds multimodal foundation models from image, video and audio data.
why_relevant: One of the strongest academic-adjacent multimodal labs.
history: Reka AI was founded in 2022 in Mountain View by former DeepMind, Google and Meta researchers including Dani Yogatama. It builds multimodal foundation models that process text, images, video and audio, and offers both proprietary and compact models. The company raised $50 million in 2023 and a $110 million round in 2024 at a reported $1 billion valuation, partnering with sovereign and enterprise customers.

name: Aleph Alpha
short_description: European AI lab building transparent, sovereign language models.
why_relevant: Champion of European data sovereignty in AI.
history: Aleph Alpha was founded in Heidelberg in 2019 by Jonas Andrulis, positioning itself as Europe's sovereign AI champion. It built the Luminous and Pharia model families and offers on-premise, transparent AI for government and industry. The company raised over $500 million, including a 2023 round above $500 million, and partnered with German and European institutions to promote data sovereignty and regulatory compliance.

name: Writer
short_description: Enterprise generative AI platform with domain-specific models.
why_relevant: Deep enterprise focus on domain-specific model control.
history: Writer was founded in San Francisco in 2020 by May Habib and Waseem AlShikh. It grew from an AI writing assistant into a full enterprise generative AI platform with the Palmyra model family and knowledge graph-based RAG. The company raised $100 million in 2023 and a $200 million Series C in 2024 at a $1.9 billion valuation, focused on domain-specific, controllable models for large enterprises.

name: Anysphere (Cursor)
short_description: Creator of Cursor, the AI-native code editor.
why_relevant: Proof that AI coding assistants can change developer workflow economics.
history: Anysphere was founded in San Francisco in 2022 by Michael Truell, Sualeh Asif, Arvid Lunnemark and Aman Sanger, creators of the Cursor code editor. Cursor integrated LLM agents directly into the editing workflow and gained rapid adoption among developers. The company raised a $60 million Series A in 2024 and a $105 million round at a $2.5 billion valuation in early 2025, followed by a round valuing it near $10 billion.

name: Cognition AI
short_description: Developer of Devin, an autonomous AI software engineering agent.
why_relevant: Pushed the idea of fully autonomous engineering agents.
history: Cognition AI was founded in 2023 in San Francisco by Scott Wu, Steven Hao and Walden Yan. It unveiled Devin in March 2024, marketed as the first autonomous AI software engineer, capable of planning and completing coding tasks end to end. The company raised $175 million at a $2 billion valuation in 2024 and later acquired Windsurf in 2025, continuing to push autonomous engineering agents.

name: Lovable
short_description: Lets non-developers generate full web applications from prompts.
why_relevant: One of the fastest-growing prompt-to-app platforms.
history: Lovable was founded in Stockholm in 2023 by Anton Osika and Fabian Hedin, building on the open-source GPT Engineer project. Its prompt-to-app platform lets non-developers generate and deploy full web applications. Lovable grew to millions of users and reported rapid revenue growth, raising a $200 million round in 2025 at a $1.8 billion valuation, making it one of Europe's fastest-growing AI startups.

name: Replit
short_description: Cloud IDE with an agentic AI that builds and deploys apps.
why_relevant: Simplified coding and app creation through the browser plus AI.
history: Replit was founded in 2016 by Amjad Masad, Faris Masad and Haya Odeh, offering a browser-based collaborative IDE. It added the Ghostwriter AI and later the agentic Replit Agent, which builds and deploys apps from natural-language prompts. Replit serves tens of millions of users and raised over $220 million, reaching a $1.16 billion valuation in 2023, while expanding its AI-first development platform.

name: ElevenLabs
short_description: Voice AI platform for realistic text-to-speech and voice cloning.
why_relevant: Set the quality bar for synthetic speech across languages.
history: ElevenLabs was founded in London in 2022 by Piotr Dabkowski and Mati Staniszewski, focused on realistic neural text-to-speech and voice cloning. Its models quickly set a quality benchmark across many languages, and the platform expanded into dubbing, voice agents and APIs. The company raised a $19 million Series A, then an $80 million Series B in 2024 at a $1.1 billion valuation, becoming a leader in voice AI.

name: Synthesia
short_description: Produces studio-quality video from text using realistic avatars.
why_relevant: Created the enterprise AI-video category used by major brands.
history: Synthesia was founded in London in 2017 by Victor Riparbelli, Matthias Niessner, Lourdes Agapito and Steffen Tjerrild, spinning research on neural rendering into a product. It creates studio-quality videos from text using AI avatars, targeting corporate training and communications. The company raised $90 million in 2023 at a $1 billion valuation and serves thousands of enterprises, including major global brands.

name: Runway
short_description: Builds the Gen series of generative video models and creative tools.
why_relevant: Pioneered consumer generative video before the current wave.
history: Runway was founded in New York in 2018 by Cristóbal Valenzuela, Anastasis Germanidis and Alejandro Matamala. It released the Gen-1 and Gen-2 video models in 2023, bringing text-to-video to a broad audience, and later the Gen-3 Alpha model. The company raised a $141 million Series C in 2023 at a $1.5 billion valuation and a $308 million round in 2025, partnering with studios and media companies.

name: Luma AI
short_description: Developer of the Dream Machine video generator, spun out of NeurIPS research.
why_relevant: High-quality text-to-video with strong physics realism.
history: Luma AI was founded in Palo Alto in 2021 by Amit Jain and Alberto Taiuti, initially focused on neural rendering and 3D capture with its NeRF technology. It launched Dream Machine in 2024, a text-to-video generator known for realistic motion, which gained millions of users. The company raised a $43 million Series B and later a $90 million round, establishing itself as a leading generative video lab.
